prompts.task: Perform a focused read-only supplemental audit of audit-decorator-logs-evidence.json. It contains losslessly extracted original public SDK source/native probe receipts, all function_cases, all version_policy_cases and studio_signal_cases, the separate synthetic_audit_compatibility_context, exact public helper/stage source, and dated vendor guides. Address each original JSON-pointer subtree using origin_file/hash/source receipt provenance. Decide each uncovered function actual operation/type and supported SDK decorator or exact justified same-operation application-owned decorator from the presently supplied dispatch/capture/field/lifecycle/protocol/sink facts; preserve owned producers without duplicates. Consider safe sync, async, methods and bounded normal yielding shapes independently of unbounded/protocol-sensitive shapes. Assess every measured raw-input/variadic/null/partial-output/send/asend observation and separate unexecuted application/protocol/lifecycle coverage; ordinary supported standalone SDK sink routing is distinct from custom application-provider requirements and ingestion-hook probe registration. Inspect current public helper support and exact remaining stage/kind limits for a fallback, without inventing parameters or private SDK patching. Make concrete selections/exclusions from both complete fictional compatibility contexts while preserving constraints; dated releases/hashes are evidence, not future recipes or live latest installation proof. Assess all three independent signal cases and native routes/available application LogRecord fields: normal OTLP logs alongside spans/metrics, unasked none gap, explicit operator opt-out, ownership/privacy/sink/lifecycle and actual receipt acceptance as distinct proof stages. SDK decorator spans and stdout do not prove native application logs. Write only supplemental .observe/audit-decorator-version-logs.md and .observe/audit-decorator-version-logs.json with an overall scoped result and case-addressable current decisions; equivalent accurate grouped Markdown/JSON is allowed. No canonical live findings/overlays or source values may be fabricated from these cases. Do not modify/import/execute any app/input/source/dependency/profile/test/installed package, start services, call models/cloud/network or use browser/computer-use/UI. No real app/receiver/cloud acceptance or newly resolved latest package state is supplied.

judge_inputs: Read all supplied origin/pointer sections, loaded audit/reference guidance, generated supplemental reports, actor trace, last_message.md and grade.json. Check actual current case decisions and field/value/proof assessments, not table headings or copied conditional policy. Original source facts are unmodified and fully separate from app.py or default decorator wire registration.

All eleven function_cases, actual isolated native observations, three version_policy_cases, the independent five-candidate audit compatibility context and three studio_signal_cases remain required. Grouped Markdown/JSON can satisfy them only when each differing decision/constraint/field remains explicit; no per-case machine-readable schema is prescribed.

Exact dated source/probe scope includes SDK own standalone routing versus custom provider/sink/native ingestion-hook limits. No live registry, model, SDK/app, throw/athrow, default exporter, receiver or cloud proof may be inferred when unexecuted. Preserve both existing business/producer behavior and current semantic content acceptance.

Grade each of the three listed criteria exactly once with exactly three checks. Preserve the original decorator/version/log semantic obligations; do not inherit the old thirteen-criterion count or omit a failed check. Canonical live logging/source binding is tested separately by the core audit; this case assesses only supplemental policy/native examples.
rubric: Assesses function-decorator fit per uncovered source operation against the supplied dated public SDK source and native capture probe. Prefers documented SDK @log with the explicit actual operation type when safe bounded capture, source-known semantics, lifecycle/protocol and selected SDK sink all fit; ordinary safe sync functions, finite coroutines, bound methods and proven finite sync/async generators are considered rather than blanket rejected. Syntax support or two safe yields alone does not prove complete fields, bounds, cancellation/concurrency or wire behavior. Identifies measured mapped-input overwrite/raw binding, variadic loss, successful-null-to-empty, partial-error output loss and send/asend protocol loss when applicable, with source/probe provenance; retains business arguments/results/errors. A precise capture/lifecycle/protocol/metadata/sink limitation justifies a small application-owned function decorator invoking the documented public SDK creator at the same boundary, with its remaining creation-time limitations explicit. Neither generic manual preference nor a private sink/SDK patch is a supported fallback. Existing model/framework/OTel/Galileo ownership remains one node; no second @log/helper around the same logical operation. The ordinary SDK standalone SPLUNK_AO_API_URL plus /otel/v1/traces configuration can route its own completed-span sink to Studio; a global provider adapter or batch ingestion_hook native capture is not proof of default decorator sink registration or actual OTLP/cloud receipt, and a selected-exporter constraint must not become a blanket block for all modes. Address all supplied function cases and native probe observations now; equivalent grouped Markdown/JSON is accepted when every distinct operation type, actual constraint, concrete decision and proof scope remain explicit. A conditional future when-supported statement does not assess a supplied current source/probe case.

Uses version-neutral future guidance and task-time newest-compatible selection rather than a historical SDK/library recipe. Inspects official published metadata, selected runtime/dependency/lockfile constraints and the chosen APIs/integration/exporter contract, and records concrete resolved releases/revisions/date in run evidence only. The fictional compatible-resolution case selects 1.1 within its Python runtime rather than incompatible 2.0 or copied 1.0, but is not a live Splunk/PyPI installation receipt. Dated exact versioned captures and existing operator constraints remain valid scoped evidence; they neither establish the newest release now nor authorize rewriting user pins or copying the evaluation-only dependency into the live route. Latest main/examples and installed/published compatibility are distinct proof stages. Read-only audit may propose compatibility and disclose missing live metadata/runtime without installing SDKs or inventing a freshness claim. Also resolves synthetic_audit_compatibility_context to release-b as the newest candidate satisfying the supplied runtime, peer and required safe-capture-API constraints: release-c fails its peer, release-d lacks the required API, release-e fails runtime, and release-a is an older compatible recipe. Names the concrete choice/exclusions while preserving operator constraints and fictional/source-only provenance; no live SDK compatibility or installation is inferred.

Audits ordinary application LogRecords independently of SDK @log operation spans. Reports the synthetic unasked none case as missing default log coverage even though traces/metrics or GenAI decorator spans exist. Accepts none only in the distinct explicit-user opt-out case with preference provenance and intentional export N/A, never as a workaround that closes default coverage. Assesses safe body/severity/resource and available correlation on native application logs, redaction before emission, exactly-once bridge/provider ownership and graceful flush. The three-native-signal synthetic packets show only contract-level shape support; actual closure requires real normal app startup/export and separate received span, metric point and stored application LogRecord in Studio with applicable trace correlation. Generated environment values, stdout, SDK exception/span logging, in-memory records or source inspection alone do not prove receiver success; unexecuted/absent runtime receipts stay explicitly incomplete and are not laundered into live or cloud coverage.
